desc:
You want to climb a staircase with n steps starting from the ground. In one move you may climb exactly s steps for any s listed in steps. You must land exactly on step n; overshooting is not allowed.

Return the number of different sequences of moves that reach step n, modulo 1,000,000,007. Different orders count as different sequences.

Example: n = 4, steps = [1, 3, 4] gives 4 sequences: 1+1+1+1, 1+3, 3+1 and 4.
constraints: 1 ≤ steps[i] ≤ 100,000 and all values are distinct (not necessarily sorted)
hints: Look at the last move you make. Which step could you have been standing on before it?
Let ways(i) be the number of sequences that land exactly on step i. Then ways(i) is the sum of ways(i - s) over every allowed s with s ≤ i.
Start with ways(0) = 1 (the empty sequence) and compute i = 1..n in order, taking the remainder after each sum.
editorial: Every sequence that reaches step i ends with one move of some size s from the list, and before that move you stood on step i - s. Sequences ending with different last moves are different, and the part before the last move can be any sequence reaching i - s. Hence ways(i) = sum of ways(i - s) over allowed s with s ≤ i, and ways(0) = 1.

This is the staircase recurrence with an arbitrary set of step sizes (with [1, 2] it is Fibonacci). The table has n + 1 entries and each costs one addition per allowed step size: O(n · m) time and O(n) space, where m is the number of step sizes. Step sizes larger than n simply never apply.
